title: Tenant Data Sovereignty: Checkpoint & Replication Protocol
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: Design and implement a checkpoint-driven replication protocol for our analytics ingestion pipeline that enforces tenant-level data residency and provides efficient cross-region evacuation. The goal is to ensure no tenant data is persisted outside of allowed jurisdictions while minimizing ingestion latency and replication cost. This ticket covers protocol design, schema changes to upstream events, enforcement hooks in the replication controller, and a staged rollout plan.
background: Current analytics pipelines replicate usage events to multiple regions for durability and fast query. We lack a deterministic, auditable checkpoint mechanism tied to tenant residency metadata which makes evacuation, legal holds, and selective regional mirroring error-prone. Several recent incidents (customer support tickets + one compliance review) revealed edge cases where transient fanout created replicas in disallowed regions before residency filters executed.
goals: Introduce immutable incremental checkpoints (manifest objects) for ingestion windows with clear residency intents
Ensure the replication controller only persists tenant data to approved regions using checkpoint evaluation prior to durable sink writes
Provide a rollback/fence mechanism to quarantine and scrub replicas created in violation within a defined TTL
Ship observability: per-checkpoint audit events, proof-of-placement dashboard, and occupancy metrics per tenant-region
non_goals: Implement full multi-cloud cross-region streaming rewrite (out of scope)
Replace long-term analytics storage format (will be handled in follow-up)
design_summary: We will attach a small residency metadata envelope to each ingestion batch and produce a signed checkpoint manifest to a central metadata store (immutable). Replication workers will consult the manifest before writing to regional sinks. The checkpoint contains: tenant_id, allowed_region_list, batch_id, start_seq, end_seq, signed_by_ingest, and an evacuation_token if tenant requests move. Checkpoints are durable and referenced by sink writes; any write attempt without a valid checkpoint will be rejected and routed to a quarantine stream. Manifests are compact and append-only to support efficient reconciliation. Enforcement will be co-located in the replication controller component with a light-weight policy evaluator and a quarantine writer that tags offending records for scrub jobs.
implementation_notes: Add checkpoint manifest schema (protobuf) in analytics-schema repo
Ingest: produce checkpoint manifest atomically at window close. Use existing windowing layer (ingest coordinator) to avoid duplicate manifests
Replication workers: add pre-write validation hook that verifies manifest signature and allowed_region_list
Quarantine stream: new Kafka topic (analytics.quarantine.v1) and a scrub worker with KMS-backed deletion keys
Backfill: tool to reconcile historical batches older than 30 days where manifest missing; mark for manual review
acceptance_criteria: Checkpoints are produced for >=99% of ingestion windows in staging within two hours of rollout
Replication workers reject writes lacking a valid checkpoint manifest
Quarantine stream receives and retains flagged records for audit; scrub job can remove them and emit proof-of-deletion events
Dashboard shows per-tenant placement proof with time-series for last 30 days
E2E test simulating tenant with single-allowed-region does not observe data persisted outside region after 1000 messages
rollout_plan: Phase 1: Unit and integration tests + internal staging cluster (non-prod) — 2 weeks
Phase 2: Canary with non-sensitive test tenants on prod ingestion (10% traffic) — 1 week
Phase 3: Staged tenancy opt-in: invite customers with residency requirements to opt-in for validation (manual) — 2 weeks
Phase 4: Enforce-by-default for tenants created after rollout date; supervised enforcement for legacy tenants with a 30-day observation window
Emergency rollback: disable replication controller enforcement flag and replay quarantine topic to sinks after owner approval
migration_strategy: Start with a read-only checkpoint proof mode where manifests are produced and validated but not enforced; collect failures for 2 weeks
Run reconciliation jobs for tenants with missing manifests and create synthetic manifests where safe
Coordinate with Data Compliance to create deletion keys and scrub schedule for quarantine items
Document manual evacuation playbook for high-risk tenants (Confluence link in links)
testing_plan: Unit tests for manifest producer/consumer serialization and signature verification
Integration test that simulates failover between regions and asserts manifest-based placement
Chaos test: simulate ingestion coordinator crash during checkpoint production and verify safe retry semantics
Load test: validate latency impact <5% p50 for ephemeral pipelines on N=4k msgs/s
monitoring_and_alerting: Alert: quarantine_bytes_total increases unexpectedly (>2x baseline over 15m)
SLO: 99.9% of validated writes must have a proof-of-placement event within 60s
Dashboard: per-tenant placement heatmap, manifest lag histogram, quarantine backlog
runbook: If checkpoint production fails: roll ingest-coordinator logs, restart coordinator, notify infra
If replication controller misroutes: toggle enforcement flag and open high-priority incident; run replay from last good manifest
If quarantine backlog growth: scale scrub workers and prioritize tenants with high legal sensitivity
notes: Design reviewed with Legal and Privacy on 2025-02-25; action item: include timestamped signature to support audits
Prototype showed <1ms median added latency for replication workers in our staging cluster
We decided against per-record cryptographic markers to avoid CPU overhead; checkpoint manifests are signed at window level
Consider follow-up: tie manifests to long-term retention policy enforcement (retention-tag field)
